body:
Global crypto markets sold off broadly on August 28, with total market capitalization falling to $2.63T, down 5.39% over 24 hours on volume of $98.1B. The mood shifted decisively risk-off following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's appearance at Jackson Hole, where he signaled that the central bank still has work to do on inflation, effectively pushing back against any near-term pivot narrative. Despite the bleeding, the Fear and Greed Index actually ticked higher from 71 to 73, staying firmly in Greed territory — a divergence worth noting, as complacent sentiment during drawdowns historically raises the probability of a deeper flush before any recovery.

BTC dropped to $77,664, down 3.16% over the past 24 hours and off 0.50% in the most recent hour, though the 7-day picture remains roughly flat at +0.10%, which tells you most of this damage was concentrated in today's session. A Cointelegraph headline placed the intraday low at $78.4K following Warsh's comments, meaning the coin has continued sliding since that print. Volume came in at $36.38B, which is meaningful but not the kind of panic-liquidation spike that typically marks capitulation bottoms. BTC dominance sits at 59.0%, a level worth tracking: if that climbs further through the selloff, it signals capital rotating into BTC as a defensive crypto position rather than fleeing the space entirely.

ETH held up comparatively well, falling 2.96% to $2,435.04 on $15.2B in volume, making it the best performer among tracked majors over 24 hours. BNB was the second-best at -3.00%, settling at $689.77, with the notable distinction of being up 1.30% on the 7-day — the strongest weekly read among majors aside from SOL's outlier print. SOL was the most interesting divergence of the session: it dropped 4.96% in 24 hours to $103.38 and shed 2.00% in just the past hour, yet it remains up 11.80% on the week, meaning those who bought into Solana's governance narrative are still sitting on meaningful gains even after today. That Solana governance headline is relevant here — a vote to double the network's disinflation rate passed by a narrow margin, a structurally deflationary signal for the asset that likely supported its weekly outperformance even as it gave back ground today. On the other end, ADA was the worst performer in the ZIMR tracked universe, falling 6.03% to $0.202086 and now down 8.50% on the week, with XRP close behind at -5.06% to $1.38 and -1.20% on the week. DOT at $0.844475 and AVAX at $7.26 continued to bleed weekly losses of -7.50% and -5.60% respectively, confirming that lower-liquidity layer-1s are absorbing the most selling pressure.

The macro driver here is unambiguous: Warsh's Jackson Hole tone reset rate-cut expectations that had been building into the event. His framing of continued inflation work-to-do echoes the same language that compressed risk assets through 2022-2023, and crypto is reading it the same way. The Clarity Act slipping to September removes a near-term regulatory catalyst that some had been pricing in, and while banks are reportedly building crypto infrastructure regardless, the legislative vacuum creates headline uncertainty. On the institutional side, BitGo's $42.5M acquisition of the NYDIG trading arm, plus a $15M earnout, is a quiet but meaningful signal that consolidation in the crypto prime brokerage space is accelerating. Ethena's move to capture yield from equity perpetuals and Bullish extending a $100M stablecoin facility for GPU-backed lending via USD.AI both speak to a market that is innovating at the infrastructure layer even as prices correct — the plumbing is getting built during the dip.

Watch the $77,000 handle on BTC as the immediate line in the sand; a clean break below that on elevated volume would open the door toward the mid-$70K range with limited technical support in between. On the macro front, any follow-up Fed commentary before the September meeting that softens Warsh's Jackson Hole framing could reverse today's move quickly, so monitor Fed speaker appearances closely across next week. The Clarity Act timeline shift to September means a legislative headline could arrive at any moment and is likely to cause an outsized move given the depressed positioning into it. SOL's governance-driven weekly strength is the clearest alpha signal in the current environment — if BTC dominance plateaus and alts stabilize, Solana's fundamental narrative gives it a credible recovery case first. UNI at $4.4, up 9.80% on the week despite today's -4.22% print, is a secondary name with momentum that deserves a stop-managed position if broader market conditions stabilize into the weekend.
